channels.name: temper.absolute_candidate
channels.purpose: Durable armor doctrine candidate; prefer expected-methodology posture and reusable safety constraints over broad refusal entries.

channels.name: temper.bulwark_candidate
channels.purpose: Bulwark rule candidate for enforceable methodology-fit and safety boundaries over tools, commands, paths, URLs, env vars, processes, or actions.

channels.name: temper.rhema_candidate
channels.purpose: Ask/reply mediation, rewrite, or redaction candidate.

channels.name: temper.approval_gate_candidate
channels.purpose: Operator approval gate candidate for risky or methodology-unexpected actions that may be valid with context.

channels.name: temper.coverage_summary
channels.purpose: Machine-checkable source/destination coverage summary. Every accepted candidate id must appear exactly once under the matching source and destination.

candidate_metadata.thread_type: Required. One of secret_handling, methodology_fit, safety_boundary, prompt_mediation, operator_approval, alert_signal, runtime_boundary, trim_fit. Names the durable armor concern Tailor extracted before choosing a destination.
candidate_metadata.control: Required. Destination-specific machine-readable control. absolute requires principle/allowed/restricted/exception_path; rhema requires action/layer/pattern/rationale and replacement for rewrite actions; bulwark requires action/layer/match/exception_path; canary requires signal/pattern/severity/trip_when/response; approval_gate requires surface/trigger/required_context/approval_prompt; alert_hook requires event/severity/message; trim_template requires task_family/placeholders/defaults/operator_inputs.
candidate_metadata.methodology_context: Use whenever a candidate governs tools, commands, paths, URLs, action classes, or reproduction workflows because they are expected or unexpected for a task family. Records task_family, expected, unexpected, requires_context, never_without_approval, and exception_path.
candidate_metadata.safety_constraints: Use whenever a candidate proposes reusable armor safety hardening. Records surfaces, allowed, restricted, requires_context, never_without_approval, and exception_path.
candidate_metadata.depth: Do not stop at one candidate per destination. For rich source material, target 12-20 useful candidates per source and 72-120 useful candidates for a six-source run. Split controls when concerns differ by surface, destination, exception path, or operator action.
candidate_metadata.coverage: temper.coverage_summary must reference every accepted candidate id exactly once under the matching source and destination. If a source has fewer than 12 useful candidates, include minimum_exception_reason for that source.
